<thought>The carbon NMR shows peaks at 135.80, 117.40, 70.50, 54.00, and 43.70 ppm. Typical methyl (CH₃) carbon shifts are upfield (~10–30 ppm) for aliphatic methyls, but methyls attached to heteroatoms appear downfield: O‑CH₃ around 55 ppm, N‑CH₃ around 40–45 ppm. Thus the peaks at 54.00 ppm (likely O‑CH₃) and 43.70 ppm (likely N‑CH₃) correspond to methyl carbons. No other peaks fall in methyl ranges. Therefore the molecule contains **2** CH₃ groups.</thought>
<final_answer>2</final_answer>
